newsitem.title: USA: Markets take Russian security chief's firing in stride.
newsitem.headline: Markets take Russian security chief's firing in stride.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's unexpected decision to fire Russian security chief Alexander Lebed sent mild shivers through U.S. financial markets Thursday, but experts said any sustained moves will require clearer signals about the Russian political outlook.
The dollar jumped to a 4-1/2-month high of 1.5454 German marks on the news, before paring gains to trade at 1.5430 in late afternoon.

"It was a reason to buy dollars, but I don't think it's a reason for sustained dollar strength by any means, and I wouldn't be surprised to see a slip back to where we were before this thing happened," said Earl Johnson, foreign exchange economist at the Bank of Montreal.
Dollar-denominated Russian Vneshekonombank loans fell as much as 2-1/2 points immediately following the announcement of Lebed's firing before rebounding to trade down 1-3/4 points.
The stock market stayed on its bull track, showing little pullback on the Russian development.

Oil prices were higher, but analysts said the market's attention was elsewhere, with the focus remaining on the short supply of heating oil in the United States and Europe ahead of winter. Crude oil was up 23 cents at $25.40 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange.

Experts said the markets will keep a close eye on Russian political developments in the months to come. Yeltsin is scheduled to undergo heart surgery in mid-November and the succession battle is likely to heat up.
For investors, the key question remains who would come into power if Yeltsin were to step down or was no longer able to fulfil his presidential duties, analysts said.
The Lebed firing "certainly has the potential to be disruptive, but I don't really think it has that much significance yet," said Jack McIntyre, an energy analyst at McCarthy Crisanti Maffei.
